title: Queen against pawn
line: Usually the queen wins. With a bishop or rook pawn on the seventh, it may not.

steps.text: The queen has driven the black king in front of its own pawn. While it stands there, the pawn cannot move.
That gives you a free move. Bring your king one step closer.

also.g6g5: That is a step closer too. This lesson takes the other one.
also.g6f6: That works too, though it is not a step closer. This lesson steps toward the pawn.

steps.hint: Step the king toward the pawn.
steps.after: Each time the king blocks its pawn, your king gets a step nearer.

steps.text: The king stepped aside, and the pawn is pinned. Keep the pin, and also guard the square in front of the pawn.

also.g2f2: That keeps the pin too, and it works. This lesson also guards the square in front of the pawn.
also.g2h2: That keeps the pin too, and it works. This lesson also guards the square in front of the pawn.

steps.hint: Stay on the pawn's row, right next to it.
steps.after: The pawn is still pinned, and the square in front of it is yours. Now your king can walk up.

steps.text: A bishop pawn, on the c-file or the f-file, can draw when the white king is far. Here, if the queen takes the pawn, it is stalemate.
A rook pawn can draw the same way. Here the queen has taken the last free squares, and Black, to move, is stalemated.
You have Black, with a bishop pawn, and you are in check. Leave the pawn and step toward the corner.

also.b2a3: That holds too here, because the white king is so far away. This lesson heads for the corner.
also.b2c1: That holds too here, because the white king is so far away. This lesson heads for the corner.
also.b2c3: That holds too here, because the white king is so far away. This lesson heads for the corner.

steps.hint: The edge file, toward the corner.
steps.after: Once your king is in the corner, taking the pawn leaves it no move, and the white king is too far to help.

summary: The queen forces the king in front of its pawn and her king comes closer. Bishop and rook pawns may hold.
